summary: HR user management with email invites
description: HR Admin adds a person by email, picks their role and manager, and the person gets an email with a link to set their own password (no password is ever emailed); first sign-in goes to the set-password page. HR can also change a person's manager and role. Additive: the three docs roles stay; the PRD gives HR Admin only policies and audit, so this extends what an HR Admin does and is confirmed with the supervisor before it ships. PRD US-04 AC2 already expects an org-chart change to move pending requests to the new manager. Parked earlier in the handoff (invite flow, SMTP, service-role key). Needs, from the user: an SMTP account in Supabase (a verified sender; the demo uses a throwaway sender, see TASK-045) and the Supabase service-role key as a SERVER-ONLY Vercel variable. Supabase's built-in sender only delivers to project team members at 2 messages per hour; custom SMTP lifts that to 30 per hour by default (adjustable). Deactivating leavers is out of this epic (backlog).

summary: Decision record, SMTP runbook and server-only service key
description: A new file docs/arch-docs/ADR-LeaveTrack-E004-User-Management.md (ADR-E003 is not edited; it says the service-role key is never an app variable, so E004 records the one deliberate exception: a server-only SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY used only by HR-only route handlers through src/lib/supabase/admin.ts, never imported by client code, never logged, never NEXT_PUBLIC). Add the variable to src/lib/env.ts (required in production for the handlers that need it, never exposed) and .env.example with a comment; extend security-guards.test.ts so the key cannot reach a client bundle. Runbook knowledge/runbooks/smtp-and-invites.md: the Supabase custom SMTP settings, the rate limit, the invite email template, Site URL and redirect URLs, and the options: for the demo a dedicated Gmail account with an app password (smtp.gmail.com, no domain needed; for non-production use only), for production a provider with a verified domain (Brevo's own Supabase guide requires domain authentication; Resend's free plan was reported to send only to the account owner, check before choosing). A demo fallback that needs no email: HR copies a generated invite link (documented as demo-only, since the link grants access). The user does the dashboard and Vercel steps; the code and runbook are ours.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: the ADR names the key, where it may be used and why;AC2: the key is read only through getEnv(), is in .env.example, and a test fails if it appears in client code or a NEXT_PUBLIC variable;AC3: the runbook lets the user configure SMTP and send a test invite to a throwaway address;AC4: no secret is committed or logged

summary: Migration: user audit trail and must_change_password
description: One migration (never edit an applied one; update types.ts in the same change): table user_audit (id, actor_id, target_user_id, action created, role_changed, manager_changed, detail jsonb limited to non-secret fields, occurred_at) with RLS deny-by-default, an index on target_user_id and occurred_at, and append-only and no-truncate triggers like audit_log (audit_log cannot be used because its leave_request_id is required). Add users.must_change_password boolean not null default false (true for an invited person until they set a password). No hard delete of users. Seed stays idempotent. Verify script probes and a gated real-database test with mutations.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: user_audit rows can be inserted but never updated, deleted or truncated;AC2: users.must_change_password exists, defaults to false and existing users are unaffected;AC3: types.ts mirrors the migration and the schema verification passes;AC4: the seed runs twice with no change

summary: Add a person: invite route handler
description: POST /api/users, wrapped in withErrorHandling, hr_admin only, zod body { email, name, role (employee | manager | hr_admin), manager_id (optional, must be an existing manager or hr_admin user, never the person themselves) }. Uses src/lib/supabase/admin.ts (service key, server-only) to invite the email (Supabase inviteUserByEmail with redirectTo to the app's /auth/confirm) and, in one sql.begin, inserts the users row (lower(email) unique), must_change_password = true and a user_audit row. Order and failure: create the database row and audit in one transaction first, call the invite after, and if the invite fails mark nothing half-done (a retry with the same email is idempotent and re-sends; an email already in users is a CONFLICT, never a duplicate). Never accept a client user id; never return the invite link in the normal response; log only the target user id. Tests with a fake admin client: scope (manager and employee refused), duplicate email, invalid manager, role validation, the invite failure path, audit row in the same transaction.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: an HR Admin adds a person with an email, name, role and manager, the users row and a user_audit row are written in one transaction and the invite is requested;AC2: a manager or employee gets 403;AC3: a duplicate email is a CONFLICT and a retry after a failed invite does not create a second row;AC4: an unknown, self or non-approver manager is a validation error;AC5: no secret, link or password appears in a response or a log

description: A route /auth/confirm that verifies the emailed token (verifyOtp) server-side and signs the person in; then the page /set-password (labelled fields, show/hide, min length per Supabase policy, role=alert errors) that calls auth.updateUser and clears users.must_change_password in a route handler; getSession exposes mustChangePassword and requireSession sends such a person to /set-password from every page and API answer until it is cleared (no change to proxy.ts unless proven necessary; documented). The same page serves a voluntary password change from the account menu (this is the open TASK-026). Safe redirects via safeNextPath(); an expired or reused link shows a clear message and a way to ask HR for a new invite. Tests incl. a person with must_change_password reaching another page is redirected and an API call is refused.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: the emailed link signs the person in and sends them to set a password before anything else;AC2: until the password is set every page redirects and every API call is refused for that person;AC3: after setting it the flag is cleared and the dashboard opens;AC4: an expired or reused link says so clearly;AC5: a signed-in person can change their password later from the account menu

summary: Manage people: list, change manager, change role
description: Server page /people (hr_admin only, nav item for HR Admin only): a paged, searchable list (name, email, role, manager) read in one statement, and two writes through route handlers, each in one transaction with a user_audit row: PATCH /api/users/[id]/manager (new manager must be a manager or hr_admin, never the person, no cycles) and PATCH /api/users/[id]/role. Guards in the SQL: an HR Admin cannot remove the last hr_admin role or their own admin role, and a role change does not delete or hide any leave record. A manager change moves the person's pending requests to the new manager's queue automatically (the queue is scoped by manager_id: PRD US-04 AC2), covered by a test. Roles stay the three docs roles.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: an HR Admin sees every person and can search by name or email;AC2: changing a manager moves that person's pending requests to the new manager's queue and out of the old one;AC3: a person cannot be their own manager and a cycle is refused;AC4: the last hr_admin and the caller's own admin role cannot be removed;AC5: every change writes a user_audit row in the same transaction and a manager or employee gets 403

description: On /people a form (email, name, role, manager picked from existing managers) that posts to TASK-047, with field labels, role=alert errors, a clear success state ('Invite sent to ...') and a failure state that says whether the person was created but the email failed, with a Resend action. Mobile first, 44px targets. Client component only for interactivity.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: HR adds a person from the form and sees a success message;AC2: a duplicate email and an invalid manager show a clear error on the form;AC3: if the email could not be sent the form says the person exists and offers Resend;AC4: no horizontal scroll at 375 and 320 px and every field has a label

summary: User management: security review, end-to-end and validation
description: Security review of the new surface: the service key never reaches a client bundle or a log, every handler is HR-only and validated, no user id from the client is trusted, redirects are safe, invites and links cannot be used twice, rate limits considered (Supabase custom SMTP defaults to 30 emails per hour). End to end against a real Postgres and a fake Auth server (the TASK-025 method): add, set password, sign in, change manager, change role; scoping with Leo. Full quality gate, browser check, retro.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: the review finds no secret in client code or logs and every handler refuses the wrong role;AC2: the end-to-end flow passes, including the forced password change;AC3: the quality gate passes;AC4: a real invite to a throwaway address is received and its link works (the user does this live step)
